docs.hudScreens.component: THE PIECES TOGETHER, as screens rather than as rows of samples.
A row of one of everything shows that the parts exist. It does not show that they FIT — that a
badge beside a button reads as one bar, that a dialog's heading, choice, slider and actions stack
into something a player recognises. These three are what a game actually puts on a table.
import { panel, toggles, slider, button, badge, label } from "game-kit"
const dialog = panel("pause", { bounds: rect(3.2, 2.2), title: t("paused"), layout: "column" })
Which segment is on, where the knob sits, what the count says — all of it is the game's, and the
nodes are built FROM it. A toggle that remembered its own on-ness would be a second answer to a
question that already has one, and the day the two disagreed the screen would be right and the
## None of them is a new atom
A label is `Bounded` + `Labeled`. A badge is that with a surface. A toggle is a button that stays
pressed. A panel is a container carrying a title on a node of its own — because a caption is drawn
in the middle of its area, and a heading belongs at the top. There is no new capability to learn.
